heading: Give values a name
body:
A value written in several places changes in one place and stays old in the others. A bare number such as `20` does not say what it means. So Tachyon asks you to give such values a name.

The build refuses, with `TY1330`:

- a text or a number, other than 0, 1 and -1, that appears twice or more in one class;
- a number, other than 0, 1 and -1, in a condition: next to `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`, `<=` or `>=`, or inside the condition of `if`, `while`, `unless`, `until` or `guard`.

A value is named when it is the whole value of a declaration: a class constant, a field, a local variable or a default value, also inside a list or a map. A method that only returns the value names it too. The empty text, annotation arguments, imports, models and entities (their defaults are data) and test code are not checked, and text that you use once, such as a log message, is fine.

The help shows a class constant in your language:

| Language | Class constant |
| --- | --- |
| JavaScript | `static CART_CHANGED = 'cart:changed';` |
| TypeScript | `static readonly CART_CHANGED = 'cart:changed';` |
| Python, Ruby | `CART_CHANGED = 'cart:changed'` in the class body |
| PHP | `private const CART_CHANGED = 'cart:changed';` |
| Java | `private static final String CART_CHANGED = "cart:changed";` |
| Kotlin | `companion object { const val CART_CHANGED = "cart:changed" }` |
| C# | `private const string CartChanged = "cart:changed";` |
| F# | `static let cartChanged = "cart:changed"` in the type |
| Swift | `static let cartChanged = "cart:changed"` |
| Dart | `static const cartChanged = 'cart:changed';` |
| Rust | `const CART_CHANGED: &str = "cart:changed";` in the `impl` block |
| Go | `func (CartService) cartChanged() string { return "cart:changed" }` |

Often there is a shorter fix. When two methods build the same map, move the map into one private method. When one method passes the same value three times, put it in a local variable first.

This check is new, so you can turn it off for one side of the app while you move code. For Tac code, set `tac.constants.check` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`. For Yon code, set `constants.check` to `false` in `server/application.json`. Use these settings only for migration. `ty migrate check` lists every place to change, even when the setting is off.
